details:
I was in a room recently, with my avatar limiter on, where as I moved around, suddenly the frame rate got drastically worse, presumably because of some avatar that had just loaded in.   I could try and 'sonar' it out by moving around and watching my performance as individual avatars loaded in and out, but, it made me realise that it would be much simpler if there could just be a pie chart of the 'frame time' (ms spent calculating & drawing) of every avatar currently rendering, so you could identify which avatar was taking dramatically longer and block it.

I understand that profiling features have an overhead associated, so the profiling could be something that only runs while you have the pie chart open -- performance would get marginally worse while you're investigating who the problem is, but only long enough to learn what you need to know and then turn the pie chart back off again.

I know there's already the "avatar rating" system, but that's so detached from real-world considerations; lots of people have avatars with tons of gimmicks that usually *aren't activated*, who would still show up as "very poor"; meanwhile someone with a better-rated avatar could be doing something like rendering their whole polygon budget on overlapping transparent triangles, which the avatar rating system doesn't account for.  And different people with different hardware might have different bottlenecks anyway; an avatar with a game encoded into its animators might be extremely CPU-bound on one machine, but someone with a better CPU than their GPU might have more problems with an avatar doing complicated raymarching effects.   Trying to generalize whether an avatar "is" slow in the general case just isn't as helpful as it would be to be able to turn on a scanner that can answer "who is making MY computer chug RIGHT NOW".
title: Pie chart of render time of every avatar currently being drawn
